text:
olivia: Hey team — seeing NVLink heartbeat divergence in aps4b GPU pool. ~6 nodes report stale peer lists and intermittent peer timeouts. Scheduler started moving long-running batches but we're getting client error spikes and higher tail latency. Raising a P1 for infra.

jason: got the alert. link to dashboard?

olivia: https://internal.redwood/metrics/aps4b/gpu?from=now-30m
spikes at 09:12 UTC, error 1402 (nvlink peer timeout). logs: ```
[2026-03-18T09:12:07Z] nvlink: peer 10.2.7.34 stale, heartbeat missed 3x
[2026-03-18T09:12:07Z] gpu-svc[pid=4121]: connection reset to peer(10.2.7.34)
```

infra-bot: node-heartbeat-failure: nodes=[aps4b-rk12-n3, aps4b-rk12-n5, aps4b-rk12-n7, aps4b-rk13-n1, aps4b-rk13-n2, aps4b-rk13-n4]. Automatic replication fallback triggered for in-flight streams.

priya: proposal — drain the affected nodes from the pool to force reschedule, shift new traffic off aps4b to aps4a and eu-west until RMA complete. Keep canaries in aps4b disabled.

anil: spare capacity: autoscaler shows 3 warm nodes in aps4b, 8 in aps4a, 5 in eu-west. If we bounce too many at once we'll pay burst costs. Estimated +$0.9/hr if we scale to cover immediate demand.

marta: prefer not to full global shift. Can we shard routing at mlpool level and only reroute new allocations for GPU-heavy jobs? that keeps stateful in-flight tasks less disrupted.

ken: draining commands below — will run once we agree: ```
# mark for drain and cordon
infractl node drain aps4b-rk12-n3 --reason "nvlink-heartbeat" --force
infractl node cordon aps4b-rk12-n3
# verify work queues rescheduled
infractl node status aps4b-rk12-n3 --watch
```

olivia: starting controlled drain on rk12-n3 then n5. sequencing: drain 1 node at a time, wait for KV cache warmup, then next. Priya can you trigger mlpool routing rule?

priya: on it. Adding weighting: aps4b -> 0.3, aps4a -> 0.5, eu-west -> 0.2. Applying now.

deploy-bot: routing-change applied by priya at 09:18 UTC. Canary traffic disabled for aps4b.

ken: drain started on aps4b-rk12-n3 @09:19 UTC. Will monitor for reschedule errors. If job eviction rate >10% in 2m, pause and escalate.

jason: watching latency and error budgets. Suggest reduce batch sizes for GPU inference in-flight to mitigate tail latency while moving. Patch below: ```json
{"batch.max_tokens": 768, "batch.max_concurrency": 8}
```

anil: RMA queue opened for rk12 nodes. Hardware team estimate 18-24h for part swap if it's NVLink module. Flagging for expedited RMA possible but cost impact (same-day swap + logistics ~$3k).

marta: updating runbook note: mark nodes as "RMA-pending" and exclude from autoscaler until health-probe returns green.

olivia: quick health checks after draining n3: no new error spike, 95th latency back to baseline for surviving nodes. Proceeding with n5 drain in 5m.

infra-bot: autoscaler triggered +3 on aps4a at 09:25 UTC to absorb shifted traffic.

priya: routing weights now stable. Observability dashboards show request traffic moved as expected.

jason: keeping an eye on token costs — traffic shifting to aps4a (higher-cost region) will bump hourly spend. Noting to finance.

ken: if we see more nodes showing peer stale counters, plan B is rack-level evacuation and cross-rack affinity changes.

olivia: agree. For now sequence = drain single nodes, monitor 10m windows, escalate if >2 nodes fail within same rack.

deploy-bot: canary re-enable blocked until RMA cleared.

marta: filing incident doc and next steps. I'll capture timeline and cost estimate.

olivia: thanks — will keep thread updated. tagging @oncall to follow during night shift. :thumbsup:
